races.name: WTW Willis Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Glengarriff
runners_data.note: Has gone 0W0P across 8 similar-going runs and fades in the finish; a true hold-up horse whose natural rear position is squeezed toward midfield by the volume of hold-up types in this field — finishing effort will depend heavily on how the pace unfolds in front of him.

runners_data.name: Grabat
runners_data.note: Fades in the finish across all three hurdle starts, placing nowhere, yet jockey Niall Moore (5lb claim) arrives after a quick 14-day turnaround for Philip Fenton's yard which has placed 2 from 2 over the same window — pace is unlikely to suit his tail-off profile.

runners_data.name: Minella Cyclone
runners_data.note: Lightly raced and unexposed over hurdles for John Patrick Ryan's yard, returns from 112 days off with J J Slevin, a high-calibre booking that demands respect; sole hurdles run was a 7th on Good which is thin form but the freshness angle and jockey quality are live factors.

runners_data.name: Rule Seventeen
runners_data.note: An extraordinary 1105 days off the track for Simon Cavanagh, returning with only one career hurdle run to his name (2nd on Soft); headgear (tongue-pin) is new, and the massive layoff makes him deeply unpredictable — could be anything from rusty to transformed.

runners_data.name: Scotty Joe
runners_data.note: Ran only yesterday (1-day gap) which is an unusual fitness flag even for a trainer like P J Rothwell who fires runners quickly; 0W0P across 3 similar-going runs and a fader, though the very quick reappearance could signal something Rothwell has spotted.

runners_data.name: Texas Red
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who must battle Astelia for the early lead; has placed once in 8 Good-ground runs and wears a hood (pace headgear), suggesting the stable knows he needs to dominate — being forced into a pace duel dilutes his chance but he cannot be expected to give way.

runners_data.name: Dawn Coming
runners_data.note: Consistent place-getter with 4 places from 12 similar-going appearances for C Byrnes; tracks the pace naturally in the Prominent role, wears a tongue-tie, and the 39-day gap keeps him fresh — one of the better profile fits for the contested-pace scenario.

runners_data.name: Ivatt
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's runner makes just his second hurdle start for a yard that fired 1 from 38 in the last 14 days; showed promise when 3rd on debut over 2m on Good and the prominent style maps cleanly to how this race will be run — the Elliott yard's class edge matters.

runners_data.name: Astelia
runners_data.note: The other confirmed front-runner, boasting 7 placed efforts and 14 runs on similar going for Peter Fahey; has been placed second three times in recent hurdle form including back-to-back seconds over this exact 2m trip — she is consistent but yet to win, and a battle with Texas Red stretches her stamina at 7yo.

runners_data.name: Dusky Night
runners_data.note: UNKNOWN going profile adds genuine uncertainty to any assessment; returned from 131 days off with three runs including a pulled-up, and the Ross O'Sullivan yard has 1 from 21 over the recent 14-day window — needs to prove fitness and going suitability.

runners_data.name: Hardlee Trouble
runners_data.note: Holds a Prominent style with two hurdle runs both on Good ground (4th and 7th) for James Fahey, returning from 90 days off with an amateur claimer; limited form but the style maps well to a pace-pressed race — watch the first flight for a jump confidence read.

runners_data.name: How's Ellie
runners_data.note: Willie Mullins runner with Daniel King up, placed once from 5 similar-going runs; fell last time which demands scrutiny at the first few hurdles, but the 25-day turnaround keeps her fresh and Mullins has 4 wins from 23 over the last 14 days — yard form is solid.

runners_data.name: Isthatrightkatie
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type wearing a hood (confirmed by hg:h), 0W0P across 4 similar-going hurdle runs; Brian Barry (7lb claim) has limited exposure and the combination of style, form, and the large field makes her an unlikely winner unless the pace genuinely collapses.

runners_data.name: Willows Word
runners_data.note: Two runs, two 7ths on Good for Patrick Rooney, wearing a tongue-tie; Alix Balfe claims 7lbs and the 9-day turnaround is quick — no evidence from the form or style (hold-up) that this race shape suits, and the recent run proximity without improvement is a mild flag.

runners_data.name: Neat As A Pin
runners_data.note: Fades in the finish with three similar-going runs all resulting in mid-to-rear finishes; unridden (no jockey declared in the data), which in itself is a notable concern for race-day viability — no compelling angle from style, form, or going profile.

runners_data.name: Vartry Diamond
runners_data.note: Lightly raced with just one hurdle run (7th on Good) for P J Rothwell, who saddles three in this race; the UNKNOWN style flag and single run make her deeply unexposed, but the trainer's busy book (2 wins, 16 runs in 14 days) means he is not without ammunition this week.

runners_data.name: But What About Me
runners_data.note: Returning from a substantial 511-day absence for Barry Murphy, whose yard is 0 from 1 recently; a natural hold-up horse whose position on the map drifts toward midfield due to the crowd of similar types at the rear — the long layoff and OR of 80 in a field capped at 120 makes him easy to oppose.

races.paceDynamic: Texas Red and Astelia are both confirmed front-runners in a 17-runner maiden hurdle over 2m at Kilbeggan on Good to Yielding ground, and both are expected to press for the early lead, creating a contested but honest gallop rather than a dominating solo breakaway. With two genuine pace-setters pushing each other, the tempo should be sustained throughout, compressing the finish and reducing the premium on late acceleration — this shapes as a race that will suit prominent racers who can travel within a length or two of the action without burning petrol chasing splits. Glengarriff and But What About Me are redistributed to midfield on the map but are genuinely hold-up types by nature; with so much pace in the race, truly prominent runners like Dawn Coming, Ivatt, How's Ellie, and Hardlee Trouble are best-placed to exploit the honest gallop without getting caught in traffic or burning out in a pace duel. The race shape firmly favours the prominent-to-midfield profile — horses who can sit handily without leading, track the pace through the final turn, and produce a clean jump at the last.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Texas Red and Astelia push each other honestly enough to string out the field, rewarding horses who track the pace without joining the duel.
scenarios.body: The honest early gallop set by the two front-runners will ensure the race is truly run, allowing prominent stalkers to arrive full of running turning for home without the pace collapsing into a sprint; horses with a clean position just off the pace will hit the line strongest.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse; Hold-Ups Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Texas Red or Astelia backs off or is taken wide early, the pace becomes ragged and hold-up horses are gifted a slingshot run.
scenarios.body: A messy or falsely-run race could see the early leaders stop quickly in the home straight, presenting late-running types a rare opportunity in a field this large; Isthatrightkatie or Scotty Joe could emerge from midfield if the splits slow mid-race before the final flight.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runners Survive
scenarios.trigger: If Texas Red or Astelia opens up a significant lead that rivals cannot close on the approach to the final hurdle.
scenarios.body: One of the pace-setters, likely Astelia who has strong place form from the front and seven placed efforts at this trip/going combination, stays in front long enough that no hold-up or prominent runner can close; a genuinely run race on Good to Yielding suits her stamina profile at 7yo.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Lightly Raced Type Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If a well-handicapped or lightly raced runner with unexposed potential exploits the pace chaos and confusion in a large 17-runner field.
scenarios.body: With several horses carrying UNKNOWN going tags or minimal hurdles form, a fresh or unexposed runner could exploit positional confusion and emerge late; Minella Cyclone with Slevin in the plate or Rule Seventeen on a 1105-day return could carry lightly-exposed profiles to an upset.

watchPoints.text: Texas Red and Astelia are on a direct collision course for the lead — watch the first two hurdles to see which capitulates; if neither gives way the pace could burn both out and fundamentally alter who benefits in the closing stages.

Scotty Joe ran only yesterday and returns for P J Rothwell with an unusually rapid turnaround — monitor at the start and over early hurdles for any sign of fatigue or jumping sloppiness that would confirm the quick reappearance as a concern.

How's Ellie fell on her most recent start and carries that jumping question into a 17-runner field with congested early stages — watch her jump the first two hurdles cleanly before taking her prominent chance at face value.

Rule Seventeen reappears after 1105 days off the track with new headgear and only one career hurdle run — if she travels smoothly in the early stages and jumps fluently, the freshness premium could make her dangerous despite the paper form looking thin.

The sheer size of the 17-runner field on a tight Kilbeggan circuit increases the probability of traffic incidents between the last two hurdles — horses drawn or tracking wide with clear daylight (Ivatt, Dawn Coming) will have a notable positional advantage over those forced to wait for gaps.

races.name: Séan Daly Memorial Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Hopes Are High
runners_data.note: Lightly raced 4yo with a strong record on similar going (2 wins, 5 places from 10 runs) and a consistent recent form string including back-to-back wins; natural hold-up style suits a race run at genuine pace, and 37 days off the track is not a concern given the trainer's 1 from 8 recent record is modest but the horse arrives in career-best form.

runners_data.name: Splashing Out
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old veteran with solid course-and-distance profile and blinkers/hood combination suggesting a horse that needs to be switched on; genuine hold-up racer who has won twice at this trip on good ground and a 22-day break is ideal — apprentice jockey Peter Smithers (5) claims 5lbs which helps offset a 164lb burden.

runners_data.name: Speisialta
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner wearing a hood and cheekpieces, who won over this trip on soft 9 days ago and has strong form at this sort of pace — will go forward immediately and fight for the lead against Rosenborg, making him the key pace influence in shaping how this race is run.

runners_data.name: Cocofred
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead-trained 5yo who carries prominent-racing style and won over this exact distance on good ground in latest start; 60-day break is the main query but De Bromhead's team arrived with 6 winners from 29 in the last fortnight suggesting horses are in good order — Darragh O'Keeffe is a significant booking.

runners_data.name: Migdam
runners_data.note: Modest recent form with no wins from the last five starts and a 119-day absence is a significant concern; going record on similar conditions is uninspiring (1 win, 2 places from 15 runs) and this hold-up operator has been well beaten at shorter distances than today's 2m, making him difficult to recommend.

runners_data.name: My Trump Card
runners_data.note: Form string reads 60-068 and this horse has produced nothing on good ground from 15 attempts (0 wins, 0 places); a genuine hold-up specialist whose natural rear position is unavailable in this pace-heavy field, meaning he is likely to race out of role in midfield — the combination of poor form and positional compromise makes this a tough ask.

runners_data.name: Hopeful Hero
runners_data.note: Hood-wearing 5yo from T Hogan's yard who posted a win over 17f on good ground two starts back and ran with credit in the Cheltenham Festival prep races; prominent style is perfectly suited to a genuine-pace 2m race and Donagh Meyler is an experienced partner for this type of shape — 7 days since last run is fine.

runners_data.name: Rosenborg
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with a 100% good-ground strike rate at this trip from four attempts (1W, 2P) and a recent win over a similar distance 28 days ago; the amateur claiming 7lbs adds a small layer of uncertainty at the sharp end, but his willingness to bowl along from the gate makes him the co-shaper of this race's tempo.

runners_data.name: Eye Of A Tiger
runners_data.note: J J Slevin takes the mount for John Patrick Ryan's stable, which has had no winners from 14 runs in the last fortnight — a naturally held-up horse whose best run was a win over 18f on good ground, but the position he will find himself in here (midfield rather than the rear) dilutes the power of that late finish.

runners_data.name: Free Flow
runners_data.note: Consistent non-winner who races out of the hold-up berth as his natural base but will be squeezed into midfield given the number of closers in this field; 6-day turnaround with a 5lb claiming apprentice and a form string reading 7090-6 on similar going offers very limited appeal in any race shape today.

races.paceDynamic: Speisialta and Rosenborg are both genuine front-runners who will contest the early lead at Kilbeggan's 2m trip on Good To Yielding ground, creating a contested gallop from the outset rather than a dawdle. With two willing pace-setters pushing each other along, the tempo should be honest and sustained, stretching the field out early and leaving little room for recovery for those caught flat-footed. Cocofred and Hopeful Hero will look to sit just off the pace in prominent positions, meaning the first three or four berths will be fiercely contested. This shape strongly favours horses who can travel prominently or just off the pace and pick up fluently at the business end — hold-up horses relying on a late swoop face a harder task when the gallop is genuine and the field is already strung out. The field contains more hold-up types than can realistically get to the rear in an organised fashion — My Trump Card, Eye Of A Tiger, and Free Flow are all genuine closers but are likely to end up shuffled into a congested midfield rather than finding their natural rhythm off a true back-marker position, with Speisialta and Rosenborg most certain to secure the front two slots.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Duel, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Speisialta and Rosenborg push each other through a genuine gallop and the race is run to suit those travelling prominently behind the pace.
scenarios.body: The contested lead set by both front-runners creates an honest tempo that stretches the field and rewards horses who travel smoothly in the slipstream — Cocofred and Hopeful Hero are ideally placed to pounce when the pace-setters weaken. Good To Yielding ground on this sharp 2m track amplifies the advantage of those who can travel efficiently without expending energy making their own way.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Front-Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Rosenborg asserts and Speisialta capitulates early, leaving a single unchallenged pace-setter to control the tempo and dictate.
scenarios.body: A single front-runner dictating at a controlled pace on Good To Yielding ground gives Rosenborg the chance to conserve energy and deliver his own challenge from a position of comfort. Horses who can travel in a pocket just off a solo leader — Hopeful Hero and Cocofred — remain dangers, but the leader gets first run and a tactical advantage throughout.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Outpaced
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong enough to string the field out and the genuine closers find themselves unable to land a meaningful blow from midfield.
scenarios.body: My Trump Card, Eye Of A Tiger, and Free Flow are natural hold-up horses but are mapped into midfield here due to race shape congestion, meaning none will secure an ideal position and all three face being caught in traffic at a crucial stage. The real winners in this shape are the prominent-to-mid movers like Hopes Are High or Splashing Out who find the tempo honest enough to create clear gaps in the straight.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tempo Collapses Late
scenarios.trigger: If neither front-runner sustains the gallop to the final flight and the pace falters dramatically in the home straight.
scenarios.body: A late collapse in tempo would theoretically open the door for hold-up horses to swoop, but given the redistribution of My Trump Card, Eye Of A Tiger, and Free Flow into midfield rather than their natural rear positions, they are unlikely to be travelling sweetly enough to fully capitalise. Splashing Out or Hopes Are High, with their strong closing form on similar ground, remain the most likely beneficiaries even in this unlikely scenario.

watchPoints.text: Speisialta and Rosenborg will both try to lead from flag-fall — watch the first two furlongs to see which gives way, as the one who gets outbattled will drop sharply in efficiency and become a fading influence on the shape.

Cocofred has had 60 days off the track; watch the market drift or hold in the final hour, as a De Bromhead-trained prominent racer who enjoyed a sharp bounce-back win last time out could be vulnerable to undercooked fitness at this pace level.

My Trump Card, Eye Of A Tiger, and Free Flow are all genuine hold-up horses who will struggle to get to their natural position — if they are seen fighting for space in the first mile rather than settling, discount them further than their already modest recent form suggests.

Good To Yielding at Kilbeggan across all seven races on the card — conditions are consistent and unlikely to change, but watch for any variance in official going reports as the evening progresses given that ground softening late in the card could extend the stamina advantage for hold-up types slightly.

Hopeful Hero's hood and prominent style make him one to watch for early position — if Donagh Meyler gets him slotted in third or fourth behind the two leaders without using energy, he becomes a serious tactical threat heading to the final flight.

races.name: Séan Hughes Memorial 110 Series Final Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Mighty Berkshire
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up performer with a win and three places from nine runs on similar going — Kevin Healy's 7lb claim is a real asset in this OR=112 top weight scenario, and the 21-day break looks fine; tongue tie and hood applied, and his 3m+ form profile suits this test well.

runners_data.name: Cooladdi
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who won last time at 19f on Good and goes well on similar ground (1W 3P from 7 runs) — the 27-day layoff is no concern, and at OR=110 he is a serious player if he can control the tempo rather than being pushed into a duel by Keep Em Quite from the off.

runners_data.name: Cornmarket
runners_data.note: Prominent racer whose best form has come over 26f trips on Good to Soft, and two placings at that distance give him strong credentials here; Alan King's 7lb claim helps at OR=105 and the 16-day turnaround from a placed run looks positive, though a big field may complicate his position.

runners_data.name: Pride Of Place
runners_data.note: Has a win at 26f on Good and placed form at similar trips — E Bolger's yard has been quiet (0/3 in 14 days) but Pride Of Place's 14-day turnaround from a placed run and the prominent profile suit a strongly-run race over this distance.

runners_data.name: Sound Judgement
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's runner is a reliable prominent type with a win at 24f on Good and placed at 22f — the 31-day break is the only mild query, but Elliott's yard is in form (1/38 in 14 days is volume, not silence) and Sam Ewing's experience suits a galloping track like Kilbeggan.

runners_data.name: Starzov
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old with a patchy recent record including two pulled-up runs — his sim-going record is perfect (15/15) but that headline is undermined by three non-completions in recent form; Mr R Sugrue's 7lb claim helps offset the handicap mark but this horse needs everything to go right.

runners_data.name: Good World
runners_data.note: An eleven-year-old hold-up specialist who actually runs his race from the back — genuinely hard to place in a race this congested with backmarkers, and the redistribution here means he may find himself in more traffic than suits; his one recent win came at 20f on Heavy so this trip is fine, but the positional problem is real.

runners_data.name: Itsaworkinmaniam
runners_data.note: Tongue tie, genuine hold-up style, and a 2nd at 19f on Good gives him a plausible form line over this trip — Phillip Enright is an experienced jockey who will manage the race well, and a 31-day break after a fifth at 24f is not alarming, though his overall record shows just one place in similar going.

runners_data.name: Keep Em Quite
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner at only OR=102 and age five — will press Cooladdi from the start and his willingness to compete early is both his main threat and his biggest danger over 3m1f; recent form shows consistent placing without winning, and Danny Gilligan will need to judge the pace carefully to survive the trip.

runners_data.name: Priory Park
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old hold-up horse who has shown placing form at 26f on Good at this track — a long absence since a 15th and a poor recent run are concerns, but Kevin Sexton knows his way around a track and this trip suits what form he has shown in better days.

runners_data.name: Adaliz
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead's runner has strong sim-going form (2W 3P from 11) and won at 24f on Good — the 33-day break is modest and Darragh O'Keeffe's booking is significant; a prominent profile in a big field will require a good early position and clean jumping to realise that form potential.

runners_data.name: Ilbdare
runners_data.note: Won at 26f on Good last time and is a genuine hold-up type in a race where true backmarkers are crowded — the redistribution means he may find himself racing closer to the pace than is ideal for his style, and a STYLE_FIT of 0.91 tempers confidence despite strong trip credentials; Mark McNiff has been placing horses well.

runners_data.name: Midnight Eagle
runners_data.note: Won at 20f on Good and placed four more times — the note of fading in the finish is important over 3m1f, and being a genuine hold-up horse who is redistributed forward in this crowded market means his natural closing run may never fully materialise; Peter Smithers (5) is an inexperienced claimer on a horse who needs things to fall perfectly.

runners_data.name: Smallcraftwarning
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old with consistent midfield/hold-up form and an extraordinary sim-going record (15/15 without a win) — Daniel King rides and the redistribution to a forward position is a problem for a horse who needs to come from the back; at OR=95 there is a weight advantage but no recent winning form to underpin confidence.

races.paceDynamic: Cooladdi and Keep Em Quite are the two confirmed front-runners in this 14-runner field, and with both expected to press for the lead from the outset, this 3m1f handicap hurdle will be run at an honest, contested gallop from flag to finish on Good to Yielding ground. Cooladdi has recent winning form at this trip and goes well on similar going, while Keep Em Quite is a hold-up horse on paper but has a pattern of racing prominently regardless — expect both to trade blows early, setting up a searching test of stamina across Kilbeggan's flat, undemanding circuit. The field holds more hold-up and prominent types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Good World, Midnight Eagle, Ilbdare, and Smallcraftwarning are all genuine hold-up horses redistributed to midfield positions they may not naturally secure, meaning the true backmarkers could find themselves more prominent than ideal. A genuinely contested early pace over this stamina trip on Yielding ground strongly favours horses who can settle in midfield and sustain their run from two out — strong-staying prominent types or genuine mid-division travellers who are not burning petrol early will have the clearest route to the line.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Honest Pace, Stayer Lands
scenarios.trigger: If Cooladdi and Keep Em Quite press each other throughout and the true gallop exposes horses that raced too freely early.
scenarios.body: The sustained two-horse pace duel from the front ensures the race is run at a strong enough tempo to crack those who overcook it, leaving the race ripe for a horse who has settled and travelled comfortably through midfield before picking up from two out; Cornmarket and Sound Judgement both carry prominent form at this trip and going and are best placed to capitalise.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If Cooladdi secures a clear lead early and is allowed to dictate a controlled but relentless gallop that gradually strings the field out.
scenarios.body: Cooladdi's recent win at 19f on Good ground and strong sim-going record suggest he stays well and can front-run to great effect over 3m1f if the pressure from Keep Em Quite dissipates after the early stages; the Good to Yielding surface suits his profile and Kilbeggan's flat track does not punish pace-setting horses as harshly as undulating tracks.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Type Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace duel between the two front-runners genuinely burns them out and leaves a gap for a hold-up horse tracking through midfield to strike after the last.
scenarios.body: Mighty Berkshire has a winning profile on similar Good ground over comparable trips and is handled by a claimer saving 7lbs, which is significant in a tight handicap; Itsaworkinmaniam placed at 19f on Good and carries a tongue tie, and could be the one to thread through if the leaders capitulate — though true hold-up types have been redistributed in this field, so the genuine midfield runners here are not always racing in their best shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Attrition Race, Rank Outsider
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly brutal, multiple horses make jumping errors or fall away, and the race degenerates into a stamina slog with a surprise survivor.
scenarios.body: Priory Park has form at this track and placing form over 26f on Good, suggesting he stays every yard of the trip, and in a race of casualties he could loom as a dour finisher; Starzov, though burdened by a poor recent record, has a historical sim-going record and at OR=103 remains capable on his best day if the race falls apart around him.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Cooladdi and Keep Em Quite are separated early — if both press hard from the first fence the pace could be genuinely brutal and eliminate both of them as winning contenders before the home straight.

Good World, Midnight Eagle, Ilbdare and Smallcraftwarning are all natural hold-up horses forced into midfield by a crowded backmarker group — if any of them get shuffled back into heavy traffic on the turn for home, their chance evaporates regardless of form.

Mighty Berkshire carries top weight of 166lbs at OR=112 — watch whether Kevin Healy (7lb claimer) can manage the weight and the hold-up style effectively, as the combination of a big weight and a young jockey over 3m1f is a genuine factor.

Sound Judgement's 31-day break for the Gordon Elliott yard is worth monitoring in the paddock — Elliott horses returning from a month off can show freshness or freshness-related errors at the first, and Sam Ewing will need him jumping cleanly to hold his prominent position early.

Adaliz (Darragh O'Keeffe, De Bromhead) is the most notable jockey-trainer booking in the race — if she is prominent in the market, it suggests stable confidence that deserves respect given her sim-going record of 2W 3P from 11 runs.

races.name: Midland Veterinary Beginners Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Eclipse Chaser
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner; Ricky Doyle can dictate his own terms, has three placed efforts in similar going (sim-going 9/11), and 38 days' freshness suits — the question is whether his stamina holds when challengers arrive at the last.

runners_data.name: Fou De Toi
runners_data.note: Paul Townend and Willie Mullins give this horse the highest trainer strike-rate presence in the race (T14: 4/23), and his two second-place finishes at 24f show the trip suits — however, he is a natural prominent type who may not get that position here with four others fighting for the same berths, tempering his chance in a shape that needs him on the pace.

runners_data.name: Kool One
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse by profile with three wins at shorter trips and a recent win at 13f suggesting he may need the pace to really collapse over this longer 2m4½f to be fully effective; Kieren Buckley rides, and 44 days since last run is not a concern given an OR of 120.

runners_data.name: Los Blanco
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead's prominent runner (also has tongue-tie) with a strong recent record — second twice at 19f and 16f on soft and good — and Darragh O'Keeffe gives him a leading jockey booking; one of the horses best-placed to actually secure that prominent slot behind Eclipse Chaser given ride quality.

runners_data.name: Siege Of Carthage
runners_data.note: Patient hold-up operator with a win at 20f and three place efforts in similar going; Phillip Enright's experience is an asset and 22 days since last run is fine — needs the pace to be genuine but his form figures of 2-51P3 show he can be inconsistent.

runners_data.name: Some Song
runners_data.note: 152 days off the track is a notable absence flag; won at 22f on good and has placed at 22f on soft, so trip and going suit, but layoff plus limited form string (only three runs in history) means his fitness and jumping sharpness are genuinely unknown returning from a long break.

runners_data.name: The Burrow
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up type but form figures of 9/6/5/9/5 show no win or place in five runs — the lowest OR in the field at 99, and a 133-day absence further compounds concern; apprentice Niall Moore (5lb claim) may help but needs a dramatic step up in form to feature.

runners_data.name: Where Are You Now
runners_data.note: Charlie O'Dwyer claims 3lb but the horse's recent form (P in last run, 7th and 6th before that) is uninspiring and his two wins both came at shorter trips; a natural prominent type who may simply get outjostled for position in a busy early race.

runners_data.name: Fizzle Rock
runners_data.note: A nine-year-old returning after a remarkable 1,013 days off the track — his form figures of 1/3 at 20f on good going show he has ability, but this extreme layoff makes him a major fitness unknown; he races naturally as a prominent type but, like Fou De Toi, is unlikely to secure that position here given the numbers ahead of him.

runners_data.name: Manoir De Mirande
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's four-year-old has won twice and placed twice in his last four starts, all at 18f on good — the step up to 2m4½f is the key question, but his progression is sharp and Joshua Halford's 7lb claim is a useful weight swing; hg:t (tongue-tie) noted.

races.paceDynamic: Eclipse Chaser is the lone confirmed front-runner in a field of ten and, with no other genuine lead horse to challenge him, he should be able to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop around Kilbeggan's tight track over 2m4½f on Good to Yielding ground. Behind him, Los Blanco, Some Song, Where Are You Now, and Manoir De Mirande all want prominent positions, creating meaningful congestion in the first few fences and real traffic danger from the second-last onwards as riders start to manoeuvre. Fou De Toi and Fizzle Rock are natural prominent racers who have been pushed into the midfield map because there is simply more pace in this field than the front can accommodate — Los Blanco and Manoir De Mirande are best-placed to actually secure those berths given their rider authority and recent form. The single uncontested front-runner setting a measured tempo on a tight, turning track strongly favours a horse racing prominently in the slipstream of Eclipse Chaser — a smooth jumping prominent racer who avoids the midfield traffic will be best positioned to pounce from 2 out.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace, Prompt Winner
scenarios.trigger: If Eclipse Chaser sets an uncontested, honest gallop and a prominent chaser jumps cleanly to collar him from 2 out.
scenarios.body: Eclipse Chaser dictates from the front at a tempo that suits a horse travelling just behind, and the winner emerges from that prominent group as the leader ties up or is headed at the last; the tight Kilbeggan circuit gives no time to make up ground from far back once the race quickens.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Eclipse Chaser is allowed an even softer lead than expected and builds enough of a cushion to outlast all challengers.
scenarios.body: With prominent rivals failing to close the gap jumping the last two fences, Eclipse Chaser's OR-120 rating and 38-day freshness prove enough to sustain his effort on ground he handles; his three placed efforts in similar going support stamina reserves.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Deliver Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to string the prominent group out and leave a gap for hold-up horses to exploit up the straight.
scenarios.body: Siege Of Carthage or Kool One, racing patiently off a pressured pace, emerge with a clear run from 3 out and arrive on the leaders approaching the last with momentum; both have won at this distance and trip profile and carry proven form on similar going.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent congestion produces early scrimmaging, a scrambled pace, and multiple jumping errors that open the race to any survivor.
scenarios.body: Disrupted rhythm, fallers, or a concertina effect from fences 3-5 leaves the field ragged and a well-handicapped or less-exposed runner profits from the disorder; Manoir De Mirande's young age and sharp recent form would suit a chaotic race where the field resets.

watchPoints.text: Eclipse Chaser's ability to control tempo unchallenged is the race's fulcrum — if he is allowed to bowl along at his own pace without pressure, any horse racing prominently in second or third is already in the winning position approaching the last two fences.

Prominent congestion between Los Blanco, Some Song, Where Are You Now, and Manoir De Mirande in the first mile creates genuine traffic danger jumping fences 3–5; watch for a scrimmage or a runner being hampered wide that scrambles the entire race shape.

Fizzle Rock's 1,013-day absence is an extreme layoff flag — if he shows any sign of distress or jumping uncertainty early, other runners around him in the midfield group are at physical risk; Carl Millar (5lb claim) has limited information to work with.

Some Song's 152-day absence for Henry De Bromhead means his jumping sharpness over fences in a competitive beginners' chase is unproven under pressure — watch for a jumping error at a critical fence that could cause interference to mid-pack runners.

Manoir De Mirande is unproven beyond 18f and this 2m4½f trip is a meaningful step up — if he weakens from 3 out it will open a gap for hold-up horses Siege Of Carthage and Kool One to exploit up the Kilbeggan straight.

races.name: Kilsaran Handicap Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Pinot Gris
runners_data.note: Top-rated runner at OR 132, De Bromhead-trained prominent type who relishes good ground (2W6P on similar); recent win over 20f and second over 22f makes the 2m4½f trip ideal, and a 34-day break looks sharp rather than rusty.

runners_data.name: Hashtag Pretender
runners_data.note: Connell-trained prominent racer with a remarkable 13/13 strike rate on similar going, returning off 31 days with recent winning form at 16f; this step up to 2m4½f is a query but the horse clearly handles the conditions.

runners_data.name: Watch The Weather
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up operator with 15/15 sim-going strikes for Cody father-and-son combination; lightly weighted at OR 122 and proven at 2m4½f, but must travel through traffic from the rear and the 7lb claimer needs to time the run precisely.

runners_data.name: Where's My Jet
runners_data.note: Paul Townend's booking at OR 122 is eye-catching for Mullins, but the form string (60P-00) suggests a horse who has struggled for form; hold-up style needs pace to aim at and recent placings are absent.

runners_data.name: Charlie Luciano
runners_data.note: Strong stayer at OR 118 for Noel Meade, proven winner at 2m6f on good ground and consistent in the 2m2f–2m6f range; hold-up style means he needs the race to develop into a proper stamina test, but the 14-day turnaround reflects yard confidence.

runners_data.name: Soldante
runners_data.note: Kevin Healy (7lb claim) partners this consistent OR 112 performer who brings a recent win at 16f on soft; prominent style suits the race shape, though this 2m4½f trip is the longest he has tackled in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Bynx
runners_data.note: Hold-up type at OR 111 with three wins on good ground in his last five but all at 16f; Gilligan partners a horse who has consistently underperformed in steps beyond two miles, making the 2m4½f a stamina risk.

runners_data.name: Cappa Hill
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse placed into midfield on the map because the field is overloaded with rear-of-field types; OR 110, 6-year-old, no wins at this trip in recent form, and a STYLE_FIT of 0.93 means this race shape does not naturally serve him.

runners_data.name: Littlebiggie
runners_data.note: A true hold-up performer whose natural position at the back has been displaced by the field's abundance of similar types — mapped to midfield but unlikely to settle there comfortably; nine-year-old at OR 110 who has not won beyond 2m1f in recent runs.

runners_data.name: Typical Thomas
runners_data.note: 70-day break for the Fahey-trained nine-year-old raises a fitness flag; a genuine hold-up horse shifted to midfield on the map due to congestion at the rear, and the STYLE_FIT of 0.93 confirms the race shape asks him to race out of his natural comfort zone.

runners_data.name: Butter Fingers
runners_data.note: The race's lone confirmed front runner — Ross O'Sullivan's 5-year-old won last time over 16f and can dictate unchallenged here; young and still lightly exposed, the absence of any pace rival is a significant tactical asset at OR 109.

runners_data.name: Prince Palace
runners_data.note: STYLE_FIT of 0.90 is the lowest in the field, flagging that this hold-up type is furthest from his natural role on the map; OR 104, wears a hood, and a form string of P9-057 on soft/heavy ground limits confidence at this trip and going.

runners_data.name: Grange Walk
runners_data.note: Eleven-year-old at OR 103 with no wins in last five runs, wearing a hood; another genuine hold-up horse redistributed to midfield by the field's congestion, and the age and form suggest he is likely to be looking for easier opportunities.

races.paceDynamic: Butter Fingers is the sole confirmed front runner in this 13-runner handicap chase and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, Shane Markey's 5-year-old can bowl along at a controlled, uncontested tempo over the 2m4½f trip on Good to Yielding ground at Kilbeggan. Pinot Gris and Hashtag Pretender are the two prominent runners most likely to track Butter Fingers closely, creating a small lead group that sets a measured rather than pressured gallop. The field holds more hold-up types than the race map can accommodate at the rear — Typical Thomas, Littlebiggie, Cappa Hill, Prince Palace and Grange Walk are all genuine hold-up horses redistributed to midfield because they cannot all get their natural deep position against this pace shape — meaning the race will compress in the middle, with Watch The Weather, Charlie Luciano and Bynx also hunting from off the pace. A controlled, single-pacemaker contest over a stiff 2m4½f trip on a testing Kilbeggan circuit favours prominent racers who can travel close to the tempo and pounce without needing a late sprint: horses in the P-to-M range who jump well and stay prominent are the primary beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Butter Fingers Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Butter Fingers is allowed to stride into an uncontested lead and controls the tempo wire-to-wire.
scenarios.body: Butter Fingers, given a clear passage at a gallop he sets himself, can conserve energy over the fences and quicken the pace entering the straight before rivals can mount a sustained challenge; at OR 109 with recent course form (1/16f) and a young, well-handicapped profile, this shape suits him maximally.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Horses Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If Pinot Gris or Hashtag Pretender travel smoothly just off Butter Fingers and strike going to the last.
scenarios.body: A measured early gallop allows both prominent types to race comfortably within themselves before delivering their challenge at the penultimate fence; Pinot Gris brings a strong OR 132 rating and recent winning form at this trip, while Hashtag Pretender has a 13/13 record on similar going and is proven at the level.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Grinders Wear It Down
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens sufficiently in the middle stages to expose Butter Fingers and create a true test of stamina.
scenarios.body: Charlie Luciano and Watch The Weather, both proven stayers with strong stamina profiles and consistent flat-track records on good-to-yielding, can pick off a fading leader if the race becomes a proper jumping test; Charlie Luciano's OR 118 combined with winning form at 2m6f on good ground gives him the best credentials in this scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Closers Swoop
scenarios.trigger: If a strong pace develops unexpectedly and the field strings out, allowing genuine hold-up types to close.
scenarios.body: This scenario depends heavily on horses like Typical Thomas, Cappa Hill or Littlebiggie racing out of their redistributed midfield role back into their true hold-up position — a shape that is structurally unlikely given the single pacemaker and compressed midfield; the low STYLE_FIT scores (0.90–0.94) for these runners confirm they are the least likely beneficiaries of this shape.

watchPoints.text: Butter Fingers (Shane Markey, 7lb claim) jumping: as an unsupported front runner on a stiff Kilbeggan track, any jumping error at a critical fence could unravel the entire race shape and open the race to Pinot Gris or Hashtag Pretender travelling just behind.

Pinot Gris at the weights: OR 132 means De Bromhead's horse carries significant weight in what is a competitive handicap, and if he cannot travel as fluently as the lower-weighted Hashtag Pretender in the early stages, his finishing effort may be blunted.

Traffic congestion mid-race: with five redistributed hold-up types (Typical Thomas, Littlebiggie, Cappa Hill, Prince Palace, Grange Walk) all hunting the same midfield ground, there is a real risk of interference between the second and third last fences — horses drawn wide may benefit.

Charlie Luciano freshness angle: returning after just 14 days for Noel Meade with Donagh Meyler up — the stable's T14 strike rate of 1/28 is modest, but this horse's stamina-based profile means his peak effort may come late and the pace scenario needs to develop in his favour.

Watch The Weather claimer watch: Paddy Cody (7lb) on a hold-up horse at 2m4½f requires a perfectly judged ride from the rear in a race where midfield is likely to be crowded — a passive early position could cost the horse any winning chance if the pace remains controlled.

races.name: Clarke's Electrical Contractors, Castletown Geoghegan Beginners Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Begger
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer whose recent form reads poorly (U5-U70) with no wins or places from sim-going runs; the ⚠ fade-in-finish flag is a significant concern over 3m and Ben Harvey rides for a yard with 0/1 in the 14-day window — needs everything to go right.

runners_data.name: Chanceawetmorning
runners_data.note: Active and in form (1/38 strike rate for Elliott over 14 days, won 9 days ago), naturally prominent and boasts an excellent sim-going record of 3W7P from 15 runs — Danny Gilligan slots in here with a horse that suits the likely race shape well.

runners_data.name: Moonovercloon
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old veteran with headgear (hood) fitted; a hold-up type whose sim-going figures (0W1P from 13) suggest consistency without a win, and a 5lbs conditional booking for Kenneally adds risk — has ability but recent form (647-0P) is uninspiring.

runners_data.name: My Great Mate
runners_data.note: Paul Townend takes the ride for Mullins, always a significant pointer; four wins from 14 sim-going runs and an excellent place record (10P) confirms he handles this ground, and the step up to 3m from his recent 18-20f campaign should suit this prominent traveller.

runners_data.name: Affinity Rock
runners_data.note: The sole front-runner here — will control the gallop unchallenged, which is a genuine tactical weapon; sim-going figures of 1W4P from 7 are respectable but trainer Collins has 0/13 over 14 days, and a 5lbs claim for Millar means the stable is not at its sharpest.

races.paceDynamic: Affinity Rock is the sole confirmed front-runner in this five-horse beginners' chase over 3m at Kilbeggan and will set a controlled, uncontested gallop from the front — there is nobody to press or challenge Carl Millar's mount for the early lead. Chanceawetmorning and My Great Mate will track prominently just off the pace, likely sitting second and third through the middle stages, meaning the race will be run at a rhythm dictated entirely by Affinity Rock. With Good To Yielding ground (the going report consistently shows this across the card despite the listed Good To Soft) and a mile-and-a-half of staying chase, a lone front-runner setting a measured tempo over 3m on a tight track like Kilbeggan is a significant tactical asset but creates a race shape that sets up perfectly for prominent racers who can stalk the leader, pounce jumping the last, and see out the trip — making the P-style horses who sit just behind the lead the most favoured profile.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalkers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Affinity Rock sets a sustainable, uncontested pace and the prominent pair close efficiently from the second-last.
scenarios.body: Chanceawetmorning and My Great Mate track Affinity Rock throughout, race into contention approaching the final two fences, and their superior class and finishing resolve see them overhaul the leader.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Affinity Rock jumps fluently throughout and the pace is slow enough that no challenger gets close enough to pass.
scenarios.body: Carl Millar dictates the fractions perfectly on Affinity Rock, the field is strung out in his wake, and the prominent trackers fail to close the gap between the last two fences.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Deliver Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong enough to drain the prominent runners and the hold-up horses get into the race on the final circuit.
scenarios.body: Begger or Moonovercloon, having been held up off a genuinely searching gallop, find the leaders stopping in front of them from the third-last; Moonovercloon's superior sim-going record gives him the edge in this scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Falls Apart
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors or early fallers dramatically disrupt the race shape and it becomes a race of attrition.
scenarios.body: Multiple jumping incidents thin the field and the race degenerates into a test of stamina and luck, favouring whoever remains upright and travelling at the last.

watchPoints.text: Watch Affinity Rock's jumping — if Carl Millar's front-runner makes a costly error at any of the early fences, the entire race shape collapses and the field is gifted an advantage.

My Great Mate stepping up in trip to 3m is key — Paul Townend's positioning and whether he travels easily behind Affinity Rock in the middle stages will signal whether the trip is within the horse's compass.

Chanceawetmorning ran only 9 days ago; watch if Danny Gilligan is sitting chilly or under pressure from halfway, as a quick turnaround on Good To Yielding ground could expose fatigue in the final mile.

Moonovercloon's hood (headgear marked hg:v) is worth noting — watch at the start and through the early stages for signs of whether it has a calming or detrimental effect on a horse whose recent form has been patchy.

With only five runners and a single front-runner, watch for Begger drifting wide and detached on the final circuit — Ben Harvey will need to make a move much earlier than a typical hold-up ride if this horse is to land a blow.
